topic.title: Conformal Prediction and Adaptive Coverage Guarantees
topic.overview: Conformal prediction converts model scores and calibration data into sets of plausible outcomes. This topic studies efficient computation, conditional or localized coverage, distribution shift, and the trade-off between set size and reliability. Its guarantees concern repeated coverage under stated assumptions, rather than certainty that any particular prediction is correct.
topic.whyItMatters: Prediction sets can make uncertainty actionable, but marginal coverage may conceal uneven performance across subgroups or regions. Corruption and covariate shift can also invalidate naive calibration. Useful methods must specify which assumptions support their guarantees and whether tighter sets come at the cost of weaker coverage statements.
topic.evolution: The substantive conformal representatives include 2019 work on approximate homotopy computation and covariate shift. A 2024 approach uses training-only privileged information to adjust for corruption-induced shift. Recent studies focus on localization and conditional performance; a 2026 backward-conformal method transforms scores to tighten coverage bounds when set size is constrained in advance.
openQuestions: How can localized coverage be improved without unstable estimates in sparse regions?
When is a fixed-size prediction set more useful than a fixed-coverage target?
